reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Seating dimensions, row limits, and fixed-seat rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 14958, A.L. 1949 p. 564; prior revisions and cross references to §§ 320.070, Chap. 320, and 8.655). Sets public-amusement individual seat widths, back-to-back spacing, row-length limits (with self-raising seat and doorway proviso), fixed-seat requirements in theaters/motion picture halls, and box/loge loose-chair density limits.

headings.title: Aisle routing, widths, steps, illumination, and clearance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 14958, A.L. 1949 p. 564; cross references). Governs aisle routing to exits/cross aisles, minimum expanding and constant main-floor and auxiliary aisle widths by seating capacity, gradient and grouped step dimensions, aisle illumination, and keeping aisles unobstructed.

headings.title: Exit definition, doorway width, swing, lighting, and balconies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 14958, A.L. 1949 p. 564; cross references including § 320.070). Defines "exit" or "exit way," sets minimum exit counts and aggregate widths by seating capacity, mandates outward-swinging unlocked pressure-open doors to lighted streets/passageways and separately circuited "EXIT" signs, and sets balcony/gallery exit-way counts.

headings.title: Fire safeguards, single center aisles, and small-venue exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 14958, A.L. 1949 p. 564). Requires reasonably practicable scenery/curtain flame protection and constant fire-extinguishing supply while an audience is present, plus two provisos for sections 316.060 to 316.100: constant width for single center aisles and exemption from seat-type rules for buildings seating under 180 persons.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 316.060:16915 (all 4 subsections, RSMo 1939 § 14958 / A.L. 1949 p. 564 history, prior revisions, and cross references to §§ 320.070, Chap. 320, and 8.655) and verified all fingerprints. Checked seat/row provisos, aisle widths/steps, exit definition/balcony counts, and subsection 4 fire safeguards plus single-aisle and under-180 seating provisos; retained all 4 accurate titles.

headings.title: Board establishment, appointments, terms, and party limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Establishes the nine-member Amusement Ride Safety Board (state fire marshal or designee plus eight senate-confirmed gubernatorial appointees), five-year staggered terms, vacancy filling, and four-member political party limit among non-government members.

headings.title: Representation categories for appointed board members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Allocates the eight appointed seats among small amusement ride businesses (3), fixed amusement ride parks (3), a state resident (1), and a knowledgeable mechanical engineer (1).

headings.title: Initial meeting, chairperson, meeting frequency, and quorum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Directs the state fire marshal to call the first meeting within 60 days of appointment/qualification, provides for electing a chairperson, requires at least three meetings per year, and sets five members as a quorum.

headings.title: Uncompensated service and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Provides that board members receive no compensation but are reimbursed for actual and necessary official expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 316.204:16930 (all 4 subsections and L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403 / Effective 1-01-05 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 9-member board composition, non-government party cap, representation categories, 60-day initial meeting/quorum, and expense reimbursement; retained all 4 accurate titles.

headings.title: Board powers to consult, adopt safety codes, and recommend
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(3), and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434; Effective 1-01-01). Empowers the board to consult engineering authorities, adopt a maintenance/testing/operation/inspection safety code limited to statutorily defined amusement rides (considering ASTM or other nationally acceptable standards for §§ 316.203–316.233), and make safety recommendations to the state fire marshal.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434; Effective 1-01-01). Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule under this section on promulgation pursuant to chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 316.205:16931 (both subsections, subdivisions (1)–(3), and L. 2000 H.B. 1434 / Effective 1-01-01 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified statutory-definition limit on safety codes, ASTM/national standard reference for §§ 316.203–316.233, and chapter 536 rulemaking requirement; retained both accurate titles.

headings.title: Annual inspection, financial security, filing, and permit prerequisites
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(4) and paragraphs (a)–(c), and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Bars operating an amusement ride unless the owner obtains an annual qualified inspection and documentation, maintains at least $1 million insurance, bond, or department-acceptable cash/surety, files inspection and insurance proof, and holds and affixes a department operating permit (fee capped at actual administrative costs).

headings.title: Minimum standards for required annual inspections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Requires annual inspections under subsection 1(1) to meet manufacturer or engineer specifications and follow applicable national standards at a minimum.

headings.title: Spot inspections, permit suspension, and reinspection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Authorizes unannounced department spot inspections, temporary operating-permit suspension for hazardous or unsafe conditions, and bars resuming operation until correction and fee-based department reinspection.

headings.title: Deposit of fees into elevator safety fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Directs all fees collected under this section to be credited to the elevator safety fund created under section 701.377.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 316.210:16934 (all 4 subsections, subdivisions (1)–(4), paragraphs (a)–(c), and L. 2000 H.B. 1434, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403 / Effective 1-01-05 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Verified annual inspection, $1M financial security options, permit fee cap, spot inspections/suspension, and § 701.377 elevator safety fund deposit; retained all 4 accurate titles.

headings.title: Knowing ride operation violating sections 316.203 to 316.233
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 276 § 7, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Makes knowingly operating, causing to be operated, or directing operation of an amusement ride in violation of sections 316.203 to 316.233 a class A misdemeanor (note narrower section range than subsection 2). Independent review revised title from 'Knowing operation violating sections 316.203 to 316.233' to specify amusement-ride operation while retaining the narrower 316.203–316.233 range contrasted with subsection 2.

headings.title: Knowing false statements under sections 316.200 to 316.237
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 276 § 7, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Makes knowingly making a false statement, representation, or certification in documents filed or maintained under sections 316.200 to 316.237 (archived range wider than subsection 1) a misdemeanor punishable under section 575.060.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 316.218:16938 (both subsections and L. 1997 H.B. 276 § 7, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403 / Effective 1-01-05 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed and preserved the archived statutory-range discrepancy between subsection 1 (§§ 316.203–316.233) and subsection 2 (§§ 316.200–316.237, punishable under § 575.060); revised subsection 1 to specify ride operation and retained subsection 2.

headings.title: Passenger duties to follow rules and avoid unsafe acts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1, subdivisions (1)–(2) and paragraphs (a)–(h), and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 276 § 11, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Sets minimum amusement-ride passenger duties: obeying posted safety rules under §§ 316.203–316.233 and oral instructions unless contrary to those sections or rules, and refraining from eight listed injury-risk behaviors.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for violating this section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1997 H.B. 276 § 11, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403; Effective 1-01-05). Classifies any violation of this section as a class A misdemeanor. Independent review revised title from 'Criminal penalty for passenger violations' to match statutory wording 'Any person who violates the provisions of this section.'

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 316.230:16942 (both subsections, subdivisions (1)–(2), paragraphs (a)–(h), and L. 1997 H.B. 276 § 11, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1403 / Effective 1-01-05 notes) and verified all fingerprints. Retained subsection 1 covering passenger duties and exceptions; revised subsection 2 to faithfully match 'Any person who violates the provisions of this section.'

headings.title: Short title as Ethan's Law
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1341, A.L. 2021 H.B. 369). Names section 316.250 "Ethan's Law."

headings.title: For-profit private pool insurance, registration, and proof
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1341, A.L. 2021 H.B. 369). Requires owners of covered for-profit private swimming pools or facilities to carry at least $1 million per-occurrence liability insurance (including liability under § 537.348(3)(a)), register with the department of public safety, and provide proof upon registration and agency request. Independent review revised title from 'Minimum liability insurance and public safety registration' to specify covered for-profit private pool owners and include proof of insurance on registration and agency request.

headings.title: Definitions of owner and covered swimming pool or facility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3, subdivisions (1)–(2), and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1341, A.L. 2021 H.B. 369). Defines "owner" and "swimming pool or facility" (for-profit private admission-fee pool under 500 patron capacity and over 24 inches maximum depth, excluding hotel/motel, governmental, natural, livestock, irrigation, and stormwater bodies).

headings.title: Operating bar, civil penalties, and enforcement cost recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1341, A.L. 2021 H.B. 369). Bars noncompliant operation, imposes a $250/day civil penalty (up to $10,000), authorizes separate state or political subdivision suits for enforcement costs, and defines "each day of the violation" as operational days open for business.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for intentional violations and prosecution authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1341, A.L. 2021 H.B. 369). Makes an owner's intentional violation a class A misdemeanor, assigns prosecution duties to prosecuting and circuit attorneys, and grants the attorney general concurrent original criminal jurisdiction statewide.

headings.title: Department of public safety implementation and local assistance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1341, A.L. 2021 H.B. 369). Directs the department of public safety to implement and, with local law enforcement assistance, enforce this section.

headings.title: Insurer cancellation notice and local enforcement use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (L. 2008 H.B. 1341, A.L. 2021 H.B. 369). Requires insurers to notify the department of public safety if a covered owner terminates, cancels, or fails to renew coverage, and authorizes the department to utilize local law enforcement agencies to enforce this section.

Checked Ethan's Law title, § 537.348(3)(a) reference, private pool exclusions, civil/criminal penalties, AG concurrent jurisdiction, and insurer notice; revised subsection 2 to specify for-profit private pool scope and insurance proof, and retained subsections 1 and 3–7.
